claim_text: A differentiation ordering exists among dNK1 / dNK2 / dNK3

audit.primary_source_citation: Guo C, Cai P, Jin L, Sha Q, Yu Q, Zhang W, et al. Single-cell profiling of the human decidual immune microenvironment in patients with recurrent pregnancy loss. Cell Discov. 2021;7:1. doi:10.1038/s41421-020-00236-z. PMID 33390590 / PMC7779601. — NOTE: this is NOT the paper named in the hint. The hinted origin, Vento-Tormo R et al., Nature 2018;563:347-353 (PMID 30429548 / PMC7612850, doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0698-6), DEFINED dNK1/2/3 but makes no ordering claim whatsoever. Secondary ordering claims: Huhn O et al., Nat Commun 2020;11:381 (PMID 31959757/PMC6971012); Wang F et al., Genomics Proteomics Bioinformatics 2021;19:208-222 (PMID 33482359/PMC8602400).
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, in first-trimester decidua (mean 7.24 gestational weeks in controls, 8.50 in RPL) obtained at elective termination (controls) or by D&C after ultrasound-diagnosed embryo demise (RPL), CD45+ leukocytes were dissociated and profiled by 10x scRNA-seq in 24 women (15 control, 9 RPL), yielding 9,409 dNK cells; dNK1/dNK2/dNK3/dNKp were assigned by Seurat marker-gene clustering (CD39+CD18-CD103- / CD18+CD103-CD39- / CD18+CD103+CD39- / proliferating), and Palantir diffusion-based pseudotime plus velocyto RNA velocity were then computed OVER THAT SAME EMBEDDING to infer branch order. Subset proportions were re-measured by flow cytometry in an additional 23-24 women per arm. The only non-computational test of conversion: sorted CD39-CD18- dNK cells were cultured 2 days in vitro and re-stained for CD39, in 5 independent experiments. ATAC-seq of sorted dNK1/2/3 was run on a separate, unspecified cohort. In the hinted origin paper (Vento-Tormo 2018), at 6-14 gestational weeks in 11 deciduas / 5 placentas / 6 matched blood donors, dNK1/2/3 were defined ONLY by Seurat shared-nearest-neighbour graph clustering plus marker z-scores, confirmed by flow cytometry in 6 deciduas, KIR typing in 5 deciduas and Giemsa morphology in 2 replicates; NO trajectory analysis of any kind was run on dNK cells there.
audit.n: 24 women for scRNA-seq (15 control, 9 RPL); 43-47 women for flow-cytometry proportion validation (n_c=20-24, n_p=23-24); 5 independent experiments for the in vitro CD39 conversion assay (donor count not stated); ATAC-seq cohort size not stated. For Vento-Tormo 2018: 11 deciduas, 5 placentas, 6 blood donors.
audit.n_unit: women / first-trimester decidual donors (NOT cells; the 9,409 dNK figure is a cell count and is not an independent-replicate n). In vitro assay n_unit = independent experiments.
audit.controls: Healthy first-trimester elective-termination deciduas as comparison arm (n=15 scRNA-seq, n=20-24 flow); integration against the independent Vento-Tormo 2018 healthy reference dataset to test which paths reproduce; orthogonal Smart-seq2 confirmation of Path T cells; flow-cytometry confirmation of subset proportions in a larger cohort. MISSING for the load-bearing conversion claim: no post-sort purity re-check reported for the CD39-CD18- fraction, no proliferation/CFSE or dye-dilution control to separate outgrowth from conversion, no clonal barcoding, no time-zero-matched unstimulated control for culture-induced CD39 induction, and no lineage tracing. Palantir root was not an observed cell but an imputed pseudo-cell built from the mean expression of dNKp — i.e. "progenitor first" was assumed, not measured.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: Two alternatives are each sufficient and neither is excluded. (1) MARKER INDUCTION, NOT LINEAGE CONVERSION: CD39/ENTPD1 is an activation-inducible ectonucleotidase. Sorted CD39-CD18- dNK cells acquiring CD39 over 2 days in culture is fully explained by activation-induced upregulation of a single marker on the SAME cells — a state change of the readout, not conversion into "dNK1", which is a multi-marker transcriptional identity (KIR-high, LILRB1+, granule-high, glycolytic) that was never re-measured after culture. Dissociation and culture are themselves known to induce activation programmes. (2) SELECTION/OUTGROWTH OF A PRE-EXISTING SUBSET (the canonical alternative): with no post-sort purity data and no proliferation control, preferential survival or expansion of a small CD39-dim contaminant already present at t=0 reproduces the result exactly. For the computational half, pseudotime and RNA velocity cannot distinguish "dNK2 becomes dNK1" from "dNK1 and dNK2 are independent, co-existing states that are adjacent in expression space"; Palantir's branch order is a deterministic consequence of the analyst-supplied root, which here was a synthetic dNKp pseudo-cell. Because dNK subsets are additionally documented to arise from at least three independent ontogenies (peripheral CD56bright recruitment via CXCL12, local CD34+ precursor commitment, CD56dim reprogramming), two-independent-origins is a live third explanation for transcriptome adjacency.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it is severe. (1) THE HINTED ORIGIN MAKES NO SUCH CLAIM. Vento-Tormo 2018 titles the section "Three decidual NK cell STATES" and its Methods state verbatim: "Only cells that were identified as trophoblast were considered for trajectory analysis." Monocle 2 was applied exclusively to trophoblast (EVT/SCT). There is no dNK pseudotime, no dNK velocity, and no developmental-order claim anywhere in that paper. The ordering is a later accretion, exactly as the hint suspected. (2) THE PUBLISHED ORDERINGS ARE MUTUALLY CONTRADICTORY IN DIRECTION. Wang et al. 2021 (Monocle3 + Slingshot) roots the trajectory in dNK1 and orders dNK1 -> dNK2 -> dNK3 -> dNK4, explicitly calling dNK1 IMMATURE (CD27-CD11b-, EOMES-high). Huhn et al. 2020 (CyTOF, protein) places dNK2 "along a differentiation trajectory between dNK3 and dNK1" with dNK1 as the KIR-acquired, granule-high MATURE endpoint — the exact opposite polarity for the same subset. Guo et al. 2021 recovers neither linear order: dNKp branches in PARALLEL into dNK1 (Path 1), dNK2 (Path 2) and dNK3 (Path 3), i.e. three sibling branches with no ordering among dNK1/2/3 at all. Three papers, three incompatible topologies, all from transcriptome/marker adjacency. (3) GUO'S OWN RESULTS UNDERCUT THE ORDERING: their RNA velocity recovered only dNKp -> dNK1 and dNK2, NOT dNK3; and Path 3 (the dNK3 branch) is stated to be "apparently RPL-specific," i.e. absent from the healthy integration — a disease-state feature, not a normal differentiation order. (4) GUO'S OWN STATED LIMITATION: RPL decidua were collected after fetal demise, so "some alterations of decidual immune cells we observed in this study could be the consequence of the fetal death." (5) THE ENTITIES BEING ORDERED ARE UNSTABLE: 3 subsets (Vento-Tormo), 5 (Wang, adding dNK4 "between dNK1 and dNK3"), and Huhn splits dNK3 into two clusters (c5, c8) — ordering is being asserted over objects that do not replicate across studies. (6) The 2026 review that propagates this claim (PMID 42212143) itself concedes: "pseudotime analyses are computational inferences based on transcriptomic snapshots and do not constitute direct evidence of cellular lineage relationships. Prospective lineage tracing would be required." (7) SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND: no human dNK lineage tracing, fate mapping, or clonal barcoding study exists in my searches — so no OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER or OBS_GENETIC evidence anchors any ordering.
audit.downstream_dependency: CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY: Guo et al. 2021's central disease model, the section literally titled "Aberrant differentiation trajectory impairs dNK1 cell subset accumulation in RPL patients" — the claim that recurrent pregnancy loss is caused by a BLOCKED dNK2-like -> dNK1 conversion (Path T cells falling from 10.97% in healthy decidua to 4.81% in RPL). If dNK1/dNK2/dNK3 are independent co-existing states rather than an ordered series, the reduced CD39-CD18- fraction in RPL is merely a composition shift, the word "impairs" is unsupported, and the paper's proposed therapeutic rationale (restoring dNK1 by promoting conversion) collapses. SECOND NAMED DEPENDENCY: Cheung et al. 2025 (bioRxiv) iPSC-derived decidual NK subtype protocol, which interprets TGF-beta as a "negative regulator of dNK3 differentiation" (42% dNK3 without TGF-beta vs 1% with) — reading that titration as movement along a differentiation ordering requires the ordering to be real. THIRD: Wang et al. 2021's assignment of dNK4 as a late/terminal state "between dNK1 and dNK3 on the differentiation trajectory." NOT dependent: the dNK1/2/3 subset definitions themselves and the entire marker/function/ligand-receptor literature built on them survive intact if the ordering is false, which is why this grades MEDIUM rather than HIGH.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The BOTTOM LINE of Claude's call survives — this is pure inference, no observational evidence, weakest tier — but BOTH of its specifics are wrong, in opposite directions. (a) IT OVER-CREDITS THE ATTRIBUTION. "Pseudotime only" presupposes that the origin paper ran a pseudotime supporting an ordering. Vento-Tormo 2018 ran NO dNK trajectory at all; its Methods restrict Monocle 2 to trophoblast ("Only cells that were identified as trophoblast were considered for trajectory analysis") and it deliberately calls them "three decidual NK cell STATES." The claim is not in the primary source it is normally attributed to; it is a later accretion (Huhn 2020, Guo 2021, Wang 2021). An auditor grading this as "pseudotime in Vento-Tormo" would be grading a paper that does not contain the claim. (b) IT UNDER-CREDITS THE ACTUAL EVIDENCE CLASS. The real ordering literature is not pseudotime-only: Huhn 2020 supplies CyTOF PROTEIN marker intermediacy (Eomes/Tbet), which is INF_MARKER and independent of any pseudotime; and Guo 2021 supplies a 2-day in vitro conversion assay of sorted CD39-CD18- cells, which is INF_INVITRO — a strictly stronger class than INF_TRAJECTORY. So the strongest class is INF_INVITRO, not INF_TRAJECTORY. (c) A THIRD FINDING NEITHER CALL ANTICIPATED: the three published orderings are mutually contradictory in direction (Wang: dNK1 immature -> dNK3; Huhn: dNK3 -> dNK2 -> dNK1 mature; Guo: no ordering among them, three parallel branches from dNKp). The claim as stated — "a differentiation ordering exists among dNK1/dNK2/dNK3" — is therefore not merely weakly evidenced but not even consistently specified in the literature that asserts it. Per G7 I am not loosening this to make it interesting: the honest grade is that the ordering is unestablished and its direction is contested.
audit.methods_quote: Vento-Tormo 2018 (PMID 30429548), Methods, verbatim: "Only cells that were identified as trophoblast were considered for trajectory analysis. Trajectory modelling and pseudotemporal ordering of cells was performed with the monocle 2 R package (version 2.8.0)." And Results heading, verbatim: "Three decidual NK cell states" / "We identified three main dNK subsets (dNK1, dNK2 and dNK3), which all co-express the tissue-resident markers CD49A (also known as ITGA1) and CD9." || Guo 2021 (PMID 33390590), verbatim: "We applied a high-resolution pseudo-time prediction algorithm Palantir to construct the differentiation potential trajectory of all dNK cells... We found three developmental branches where dNKp differentiate into dNK1 cells (Path 1) and into two distinct branches of dNK2 and dNK3 cells (Path 2 and Path 3). We also identified a differentiation pathway wherein dNK2-like cells with an apparent tendency to transform into dNK1 cells (Path T)." And: "To accurately define the initial cell state, we imputed a pseudo cell as the start cell by calculating the average gene expression of our identified dNKp cells." And the in vitro assay legend: "Percentage of CD39+ dNK1 cells before and after CD39-CD18- NK cells cultured in vitro for 2 days... representative in five independent experiments." || Huhn 2020 (PMID 31959757), verbatim: "dNK2 express intermediate levels of both Eomes and Tbet suggesting that they might be positioned along a differentiation trajectory between dNK3 and dNK1." || Wang 2021 (PMID 33482359), verbatim: "the trajectory of the root cells in dNK1 sequentially passed through dNK2 cells with a complex series of branches and reunions, and further through dNK3 to dNK4 toward the end of trajectory."
audit.notes: HINT VERIFICATION: The hint's suspicion was correct and is confirmed against full text, not abstract. Vento-Tormo et al. Nature 2018 exists exactly as cited (PMID 30429548), did define dNK1/2/3, and does NOT claim any differentiation ordering among them. Retrieval note: lit.py methods returned ABSTRACT_ONLY for this PMID (author manuscript, EPMC isOpenAccess=N, fullTextXML empty) and direct curl to pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov was blocked by reCAPTCHA; full text was obtained as the 26-page EPMC author-manuscript PDF (europepmc.org/articles/PMC7612850?pdf=render) and text-extracted locally, so every Vento-Tormo quote above is from the actual manuscript body. Guo 2021, Huhn 2020 and Wang 2021 were retrieved as OA full text and archived (refs/S1_PMC7779601.txt, refs/S1_PMC6971012.txt, refs/S1_PMC7612850.txt). Working files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aaa/5f46e874-56b9-5c6b-9d27-d08dbfb1d5d8/scratchpad/vt_flat.txt (Vento-Tormo full text), PMC7779601.txt (Guo), huhn.txt, PMC8602400.txt (Wang), dnk3rev.txt (2026 review). G5 COMPLIANCE: I have deliberately not reported the 9,409-dNK-cell figure as an n; the replicate unit is women. G2 COMPLIANCE: Palantir, Monocle3, Slingshot and velocyto results are all classed INF_TRAJECTORY regardless of the confident framing ("Aberrant developmental trajectory", "As expected, RNA velocity predicted..."). G3 COMPLIANCE: the absence of lineage-tracing evidence is a SEARCHED-AND-NOT-FOUND result across 10 searches, not an assumption. CAVEAT ON PROPAGATION PATH: the modern restatement of this claim traces through a 2026 Frontiers in Immunology review (PMID 42212143) which cites Guo as ref 18; that review is a secondary source and was used only to locate primary references, never as evidence. One source in that chain, Cheung et al. 2025, is a bioRxiv preprint (not peer reviewed) and I did not independently retrieve it.
